/-!
# Erdős Problem 155

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/155](https://www.erdosproblems.com/155)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos155

/--
Let $F(N)$ be the size of the largest Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev F (N : ℕ) : ℕ := Finset.maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N)

/--
Is it true that for every $k \geq 1$ we have
$$
F(N + k) \leq F(N) + 1
$$
for all sufficiently large $N$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_155 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, F (N + k) ≤ F N + 1 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: This may even hold with $k \approx ε * N ^ (1 / 2)$.

end Erdos155

review.notes: Both Erdos155.F and Erdos155.erdos_155 faithfully match the cited source. The quantifiers mean: for each natural k ≥ 1, there exists a threshold N₀(k) beyond which F(N+k) ≤ F(N)+1. The source still records the problem as open. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, verified this quantifier expansion, proved that F is an attained maximum bounding every eligible Sidon subset, and proved the k=1 case. Computed F for N=0,…,11 and checked empty, singleton, and repeated-summand cases. The source’s stronger suggestion k ≈ ε√N is accurately retained as a TODO, not asserted as a theorem.
